summary: A sync check reports in sync by comparing repo generation parity, while installed copies were stale and neither output names its scope.
A rule sentence in two command documents and their generated mirrors is duplicated mid-sentence.
Project docs overstate how many helper scripts need the checkout, and the finish gate's skip path exits zero.
Worktree claim liveness uses a bare kill -0, so a recycled pid makes a dead same-host claim read held forever.
A worktree was removed while a live session still ran inside it, so its writes landed in an unlinked directory.
A driver capability pre-flight reports fit for command-file work that the driver's own execution fence forbids.
A routing tripwire test checks a fixed list of surfaces, so a new authoring surface lacking the pointer stays green.
A test uses a fixed probe directory name, so two concurrent pytest runs in one worktree collide.
A repo-to-issue mapping is duplicated verbatim in two hand-maintained command documents with nothing checking they agree.
Wave registry reports a cross-host entry as stale, a definite verdict for an undeterminable one that frees the role for takeover.
Wave registry liveness checks pid existence rather than identity, so a recycled pid makes a dead session read alive.
Mailbox fallback tests scan the whole host process table, so unrelated processes make them fail intermittently.
Installed skills and host settings reach agents without passing through a reviewed diff, so executed copies drift from reviewed ones.
Mailbox tests use a hardcoded wave name and scan host processes, so concurrent test runs in other worktrees collide.
Several shell idioms discarded exit status or error output while the surviving output still reported success.
Reading the exit status after a pipe records the last stage's status, so a refused helper call printed exit zero.
A tool-error counter stops recursing at depth six and reports zero, which callers are told to read as checked-and-none.
Six hand-maintained copies of one guidance paragraph already diverge in wording, with nothing comparing them.
A worktree leak guard exits zero silently both when clean and when not in a linked worktree and unable to check.
Repeated --needs flags overwrite earlier ones, so the capability check can report fit and exit zero while a need is unmet.
Leaked mailbox supervisor daemons looped forever on command-not-found after their worktree was deleted, still holding the ownership lock.
A planning helper reads a gitignored map file from the filesystem, so it is absent in every linked worktree.
The auto driver cut a worktree and branch and analysed an issue whose body says it must not be implemented.
A worktree removal script decides inside-worktree with a bare path-prefix match, so sibling worktrees with longer names match.
git diff --name-only prints the same filename for a branch-only file and a newly landed file, which demand opposite actions.
A security gate prints only findings and no verdict line, so a passing run reads like a list of failures.
The finish gate exits zero on every warn verdict while the flow skills say exit codes carry the result.
Docs say the supervisor stops the moment a role is released, but it stops only after the current watch timeout.
A test skip condition infers pid 1 is unsignalable from a non-root euid, which fails in containers with an unprivileged pid 1.
A model-presence preflight greps a tag-stripped prefix, so it passes when only a different model sharing the prefix exists.
A local model status command reports ready from a version endpoint without a generation smoke test, unlike its sibling lane.
The wave registry's authority-model enum has no user-only value, so the correct approval rule cannot be declared.
Finish gate step details carry coverage evidence only for tests, so other stages' success cannot be told from zero coverage.
A test runner's rerun message asserts the first failure was a flake, though an isolated rerun cannot exclude order dependence.
A failed-test rerun re-executes the whole test step, spending minutes on a phase that cannot contain the failing test.
A test docstring claims bash rejects an unterminated heredoc, but bash warns and runs such a script.
A heredoc opener inside a quoted string makes the binary-guard scanner mask the rest of the file and report nothing.
A repo-root script imports a dependency declared nowhere in the project, so it fails under the project environment.
The spec workflow documents no rule for what happens to a feature spec after its work ships.
The secret-scan hard gate has no negative control, so nothing demonstrates it can fail.
A code-review step diffs only tracked paths, so brand-new untracked files are invisible to the review it feeds.
A planning report's top action recommends resuming a worktree whose issue was closed as not planned, never checking issue state.
A container healthcheck probes a path the server does not serve, so a working service reports permanently unhealthy.
A server imports two packages directly that its project file never declares, relying on transitive resolution.
An unmapped-worktree warning reads identically for safely delivered leftovers and for worktrees holding undelivered work.
A planning report ranks the permanent nit-store inbox issue as the next startable issue and routes it to the auto driver.
A planning report routes a charting seed issue, which forbids implementation, to the auto implementation driver.
The finish gate creates a temp file without an exit trap, so every early exit leaks one.
A control manifest records a kind field that the consuming gate never reads, implying a distinction the gate does not make.
A shipped driver is undeclared in the capability script, so every check on it returns unknown with exit zero and no fence check.
An operational bootstrap script exists only as an untracked, unignored file in a shared checkout, at risk of silent loss.
The negative-control harness is an instrument by the repo's own bound but is absent from both instrument registers.
A documented no-unicode-dashes directive has no instrument, so a change with dozens of violations passed every gate.
After an agent's display label changed, the harness suggested sibling workers as alternatives, risking silent misdelivery of work.
A residuals ledger tool has no amend verb, so correcting a fact requires recording it as a duplicate and skews metrics.
An ignore rule anticipates a coverage artifact that nothing in the repository can produce.
A ledger record command leaves a hold's reason empty, so the planner's contradiction message says no reason was given.
A wave-level driver default does not populate role drivers, and nothing warns that every role is undeclared.
A registry register call stores a driver flag but echoes no confirmation line, so an accepted and an ignored flag look identical.
A PR merge command can land the merge and then error, reading as a failed merge and silently skipping remote branch deletion.
A branch census used git branch -r, which counted stale refs from an unconfigured remote and inflated the denominator.
Edited issue comments render identically to originals, so records cited as decisions can change without visible trace.
Roster route and unread fields mean not-acked but are read as not-heard when messages were answered over the fast path.
The wave overlap detector compares only declared paths, so two workers writing an undeclared shared directory raise no warning.
A selftest reports every fixture as untracked when run outside a git repository, instead of reporting trackedness unknown.
Docs say the supervisor stops the moment a role is released, but the release check waits for the inner watch timeout.
A hold parser absorbs an issue reference at the start of the reason into the blocker list, producing a self-referential hold silently.
A gate record command drops a reason written on lines below the token and records no reason while reporting success.
Docs describe a planner exit code as assignment-scoped, but it fires on any held startable issue regardless of in-flight input.
A command's addressing rule forbids the only address form the messaging tool accepts, so its own worker step is not executable.
A driver actively used as a wave policy driver has no capability profile, so checks return all-blank fields with exit zero.
A worktree removal script's header exit-code list predates a redesign, omitting two exits and naming the old override flag.
Lane overlap detection compares declared paths by string equality and never against the grant, so two spellings of one path diverge.
A test claiming the approval gate cannot be bypassed covers a hardcoded four of seven driver surfaces.
A one-level gitignore negation leaves nested control manifests untracked, so the control passes locally and is blind in a clean clone.
A stale-check fallback of echo 0 would report the base current on measurement failure, defused only by an unrecorded earlier guard.
A worktree removal script's usage synopses omit the newer override flags documented in its own option list.
Docs say the supervisor shuts down the moment a role is released, but a released role keeps a live watcher until the timeout.
The negative-control harness reports the same unsignalled verdict when a gate's tool is absent as when the gate crashed.
An inline comment claims a pre-fix helper exited zero and reported success, but measured it exited one.
Two helpers hang forever when a value-taking flag is the last argument, because a failed shift 2 consumes nothing.
A helper's verdict value set is written only in prose, and no test pins it, so a new value would leave docs silently stale.
A hand-maintained list of canonical agent documents in the project doc has no completeness check and already missed a new document.
A binary-guard checker prints that every shelling-out test is guarded although it inspects only one static shape.
A live-driver guard defaults to the current directory, so after cwd drift it returned clear about a different repository.
A code-review step diffs against the moving base tip, so a sibling's newly merged work appears as the author's deletions.
A declared branch-protection strictness flag is measured once and never re-read, so the starvation signal can go stale silently.
Declared file lanes omit generated mirror files, so the roster overlap check cannot see a whole file family being edited.
A negative-control carve-out exempts tests whose population is derived from the tree, though such tests pass vacuously when empty.
The review step fetches before diffing against the base tip, so the moving-base diff can present merged work as reverts to the reviewer.
A soft reset to the remote main after a sibling's fetch advanced shared refs committed the sibling's merged work as deletions.
The negative-control harness can register only top-level scripts files, excluding most instruments in a library-shaped repository.
The full-lifecycle auto driver inlines its own finish stage without the nit-store routing step that the finish command carries.
Re-registering a role replaces its file lane silently, so a dropped claim reads as no conflict in the roster.
The lane overlap check misses a role declaring a directory and another declaring paths inside it, and reports clean.
A pre-push deleted-line grep pattern cannot match deleted blank lines or markdown bullets, under-reporting deletions.
A mutation harness keyed snapshots on parent directory name, corrupted a fixture on restore, and still reported all mutations killed.
A skills validation target exists but runs in no gate or pipeline, so the skill surface is checked only by hand.
Every skill's frontmatter name violates the skills specification and mismatches its directory, and the skills checker has no such rule.
Skill trigger vocabulary sits in a frontmatter key no agent loads, while the loaded descriptions carry no triggering conditions.
The negative-control coverage denominator counts instruments that cannot structurally register a control, and does not say so.
An install drift check covers one user skills directory but silently omits another that loads in every session.
A skills checker verifies a managed mirror only when the copy itself declares its source, so skipped packages read as pass.
A test timeout was tightened then loosened across two commits with no recorded reason or reversal trigger beside it.
A new negative control depended on a binary missing from the CI image, turning the whole control battery unsignalled.
An acceptance criterion requires binding to issue tiers, but no machine-readable tier signal exists anywhere.
A review command's contract says return only findings, while its only caller now requests a second section.
A mirrored source file gives no sign that a generated copy must be regenerated, so edits twice skipped regeneration until CI failed.
Review adoption was counted by a PR-body heading the author can edit, so a twice-reviewed PR counted as never reviewed.
Installed helpers symlink into a primary checkout many commits behind main, so merged instrument features were unreachable on the host.
The local verify target omits the negative-control battery, so a local green says nothing about control health.
A lane EXTEND verb actually replaces the declared file list, silently dropping earlier grants.
A coverage line reports registered controls over census rows as a fraction although one registered control is not in the census.
A long-lived supervisor keeps executing a script file that a checkout replaced, invisible to every filesystem check.
A posted detector for processes holding deleted scripts drops the pid header line, so it cannot name which process to act on.
A release updated four version locations but the always-loaded project doc still states the previous version, with no check comparing them.
A tools check accepts any installed version of a tool, so a wrong linter version reports the same green as the pinned one.
A supervise command refuses with duplicate when its recorded pid is dead, leaving the role deaf while reading as already running.
A supervise duplicate refusal was caused by an orphaned child still holding the lock, not by trusting the pid file as first reported.
A worktree removal script reports a plain git-locked worktree as a foreign session claim with uncommitted work, none of which was true.
The local verify target omits the mirror-drift check, so mirror drift is caught only in CI while local verify is green.
The auto driver writes a review receipt but never stages it, so the next quality gate always fails on an untracked receipt.
Four live documents still describe a delegating alias command as adding a review stage it no longer adds.
Four command documents instruct a commit trailer pinned to a stale model version, contradicting the harness-supplied attribution.
A worktree directory named for one issue held another issue's branch, so tools parsing the path misattribute the tree.
A worktree locked with git's default reason and no owner reads as owned, indistinguishable from a live claim.
The planning report permanently ranks the never-closing nit-store inbox as the top startable issue.
A bundled drift-check script execs a sibling file that the bundler never copies, so the bundled copy exits 127.
A revendor step reads bytes and the latest commit id in two reads of a moving branch, so the pinned commit may not match content.
A sync check's success line omits which trees it compared, so repo parity reads as installed-copy health while installs are stale.
An inventory check enumerates untracked files locally, so it reports a red locally that CI, seeing only tracked files, cannot reproduce.
A clone-stage CI infrastructure failure is reported identically to a real failure, stopping the run though no code executed.
The auto driver writes a review receipt without staging it, so the quality gate fails on its first run.
A parametrize id built from the grandparent directory name renders the checkout name for one copy, so ids vary per worktree.
The auto driver's receipt step never says to stage the receipt, so the test suite fails the whole quality gate.
A research document classifies a security tool as absent when it had existed and been wired into an ungated path.
A green mergeable PR looked abandoned while a live session was mid-finish in its worktree, visible only through a process cwd scan.
A delegated driver's approval gate prints only to its own pane, so under fleet orchestration a worker stalls with no signal to the orchestrator.
A capability list verb called four-argument functions with three arguments under set -u, aborting rows that then read as empty.
A registry register command computes its lane delta from snapshots read outside the lock, so concurrent registrations misreport drops.
A lane path containing a newline is accepted on input but printed unescaped in line-oriented output, splitting one value across lines.
Two security scan modules record a missing binary as skipped with no finding, indistinguishable from not applicable.
A CI status helper defaults to the push event lane, which is not a required check, so default verdicts describe the wrong lane.
A merge helper's stale-base guard reads HEAD of the invoking directory, so running it from the main checkout gives a refusal unrelated to the PR.
The same stale-base refusal fires when the PR has already squash-merged, a condition that never clears by waiting.
A run checker reports recognized equals events while skipping unparseable lines, including a denied tool call, as if nothing were missed.
The instrument census count is derived but its rows are hand-appended, so a newer instrument never entered the denominator.
Two census instruments whose class requires a committed negative control, one destructive, still have none.
The negative-control harness hardcodes its own repo's census path, so every consuming repo reports an unknown universe.
Census readers treat any numbered markdown table row anywhere in the document as a census row.
Public onboarding docs present an already delivered installer as future work and advertise a version with no published tag.
Two open issues state premises that current main contradicts, overstating what is missing and risking duplicate work.
The auto driver re-syncs generated mirrors only after a base merge, so a branch editing a mirrored document directly fails the gate.
The linter never reports a positive file count and suppresses its no-files warning when a project file exists, so lint green is unprovable.
The runner's own state file is counted as a scanned source file, inflating security scan coverage.
A binary-guard regex reads a hyphenated filename starting with a guarded binary name as an invocation, producing false findings.
A receipt parser keyed on one findings format can record a genuine counter-model review as no review happened.
A type-checker exclusion names a directory removed long ago, so a future directory of that name would be silently exempt.
A deleted GitHub issue is still cited as a live reference in two tracked documents.
A CI status helper resolves repository identity from the caller's cwd instead of the declared checkout path, returning unknown for reachable CI.
A receipt writer creates a file the test suite requires to be tracked, and neither stages it nor says it must be staged.
Mailbox tests leak supervisor daemons that outlive the test run and pin worktrees open against removal.
A helper's help output prints a fixed line range of its growing header, truncating the signals list and exit codes.
An enumerated instrument with pytest-resident controls is counted as having no control, because the census sees only registered controls.
A run checker's tool-item type list omits a collaboration tool item, so a failed call of that type can let the run pass.
A command document carries an inline dated measurement of the reviewing model that is already wrong.
A bootstrap script uses one binary's presence as a proxy for five packages, leaving a half-provisioned host when some are missing.
A secret-scan test scans the whole working tree rather than the repository, so a gitignored local secrets file turns it red.
The scripts inventory still documents occupied-but-clean worktrees as removable after that behaviour was inverted.
The README advertises a Dockerfile lint CI step that was deleted along with the last Dockerfile.
A census check discards row numbers, so concurrent PRs appending to the table can both land the same row number green.
An open PR and main both used the same census row number, which the census gate would have passed.
A PR diff command given a pathspec prints nothing and exits zero, indistinguishable from the PR not touching that file.
Presence-only occupancy scans return the same zero for nothing now, nothing yet and nothing ever, and are read as absence of owner.
Taking the lowest free census row number reused a retired number, which would silently repoint historical citations.
A hand-assigned sequential census key forces concurrent appending PRs to collide and renumber, and cited numbers go stale.
A supervisor daemon's signal trap runs only after its blocking child returns, so a plain kill takes up to a full timeout to stop it.
Two sessions' correct measurements of a release pointer, taken either side of a promotion, were reconciled as if one were wrong.
A code-review step diffs only tracked content, so newly added files were invisible and the review covered only part of the change.
Careful verification on one axis, such as well-argued fixture reasoning, discouraged checking other axes, leaving a population untested.
The review receipt's reviewer field is derived but stores no provenance, so no stored value can be re-verified later.
A finding queued to a session that had already exited looks identical to a delivered one, so it is silently lost.
The nit-store resolver never verifies its destination issue is open and correctly titled, and its search fallback takes the first match.
Neither the local finish plan nor verify runs the mirror-drift check, so a fully green local gate still failed that CI step.
A new unicode-dash check scans only markdown, leaving em dashes in script comments and a test docstring uncaught.
A hand-maintained claimed-lanes file becomes stale the moment the PR carrying it merges and closes its own issue.
Guidance on the repo-wide shared stash never warns that other destructive git commands lose their usual safety net, and uncommitted work was discarded.
Registry tests that start real watchers may share the host-wide process-scan coupling fixed in a sibling test, and remain unchecked.
A slate reconciler sweeps any unlaned issue into backlog, so a worker's lost lane assignment still reported clean.
A test named for an unreadable registry script only points the data directory elsewhere, so it never exercises that condition.
A PR merge with branch deletion errors after the merge succeeds when main is checked out elsewhere, reading as a failed merge.
A binary-guard checker follows shell scripts but not Python scripts run via subprocess, so three unguarded tests passed until CI.
Implementer derivation scans the whole transcript for model fields and can record a nested tool argument as the implementer.
The reviewer extractor uses the same whole-file model search that misattributed the implementer, and remains unchecked.
Subagent assistant records are eligible to supply the implementer identity, though a subagent may run a different model.
A heading-count test maps count words through a hardcoded dictionary, so a correct index extension failed as an unrecognised word.
The negative-control battery buckets every non-good exit as bad, so a control that loses its key verdict distinction still passes.
A copied model-name literal spread into test comments and docs attributing reviews to a model that did not perform them.
A skills checker's hand-rolled frontmatter parser accepts values a real YAML parser rejects, and reports ok on them.
The quiet mode read by the session hook omits the count of skipped packages, so an unjudged install reads as clean silence.
A size-preserving mutation restored within the same second leaves stale bytecode cached, so the blinded code keeps running after restore.
The README still advertises a retired Dockerfile lint CI step in three places.
A blanket json ignore rule leaves new control case files tracked only by coincidental negations, risking silently untracked fixtures.
Two offline, dependency-free hard gates are not run by the local verify target, with no real reason recorded.
The README states control and census counts in prose that are both stale by a wide margin.
A supervisor daemon recreates its deleted wave directory on every cycle, so it never observes the wave is gone and never exits.
A lane check documented as needing no git skips its grant comparison entirely when the base ref cannot resolve.
Nothing prevents two review receipts for one branch, so corpus readers double-count or silently shadow a run.
A config constructor pops keys from its caller's dictionary, silently truncating the caller's data.
A remediation string tells operators to install a package name this project does not publish, which resolves to an unrelated package.
A security module relies on an assert, erased under optimisation, as the only guard against a return shape its type permits.
The control battery reports a registered control outside the census but never fails on it, and a contradicting exclusion goes unreported.
Control discovery reads only top-level scripts, and widening it without widening the census reader would split numerator from denominator.
A timing-coupled supervisor shutdown test failed under parallel load and passed on rerun.
Two tests each rerun the full negative-control battery to read one line, doubling test wall clock as the control count grows.
A test helper keys control blocks on the gate name, which is no longer unique, so it can silently return another control's block.
The CI-dependency gate only examines the step that runs the battery script, so a second step driving the same batteries is never checked.
A research sweep's committed red control asserts a script is unautomated after a test began invoking it, and nothing runs the sweep to notice.
A prototype self-test scores a missing pytest runner as failed cases, and three review-driven protections have no committed control case.
The wave mailbox helper stores a literal dash when given a stdin-style body argument and reports a successful send.
A sweep self-test mutates an inline re-implementation for most protections, reporting mutations caught that the real source's cases do not catch.
The next-issue report renders issues blocked on a named owner decision in a spec ledger as uncertain, hiding a verifiable decision gate.
The CI-dependency gate parses an env -u invocation as requiring a binary named after the flag and refuses the control.
The vantage helper infers host placement from the pid namespace, so a container sharing the host pid namespace is misreported as the host.
Two issues' acceptance criteria name a module file that the in-flight implementation delivers under a different name.
A staleness analysis checks only remote state, so a dependency being implemented in an unpushed local worktree reads as not in flight.
The shellcheck gate at error severity cannot flag non-POSIX constructs in sh scripts, since those findings are warning severity.
An earlier issue states an unguarded shift hangs generally, but under a POSIX shell it is a fatal error, which a hang-shaped search misses.
A new control declares no mutations, so nothing would redden if a future edit removed one of its guards and a case stopped exercising it.
The wave roster exempts the orchestrator role from overlap checks by name, even when that role declared a file lane, reporting a clean check.
The mirror re-sync trigger matches only command documents, so edits to bundled repository docs leave stale mirrors that later fail tests.
The roster grants the orchestrator overlap exemption by role name without checking whether that session holds a live worktree claim.
The toolchain-behind warning drops the field naming which checkout is behind, and two sessions misattributed the drift to the wrong object.
Only part of the scripts directory is symlinked into the stable helper path, so not-installed and nonexistent helpers share one exit code.
The mutation probe applies one mutation at a time, so two mutually masking protections both report uncaught like decorative ones.
Accepted mutation gaps require only a free-text reason, so any pasted string satisfies the check and blocker categories collapse again.
A second bundled doc edit again bypassed the mirror re-sync trigger, showing the guard misses every bundled repository doc.
A retro command document twice references a second-opinion subcommand that does not exist in the installed namespace.
Several consolidation child issue bodies still describe superseded scope and already-answered blockers that the governing plan replaced.
Helper symlinks are created only when an install command runs, so scripts added later are missing from the stable path and nothing reports it.
CI runs tests as root, so a mode-bit read-only negative fixture is vacuous there, and the repo declares no such environment fact.
A Makefile annotation says the drift target repairs and writes to the home directory, but its fix mode only prints suggested commands.
A worker declared a lane from the plan before a derivation named the real files, then edited files outside the lane unnoticed by the roster.
A worker created a new file mid-implementation outside the declared lane, a case the proposed re-register-after-derivation rule would not catch.
A command document edit caused the generator to create new mirror files outside the declared lane, which no step re-declares.
The ignored-additions check only warns at exit zero when newly staged files are gitignored, letting a runtime-required file ship missing.
The instrument census has no representation for a retired instrument, so retiring one row requires several ad hoc artifacts to keep parsers agreeing.
The merge completeness check compares against an unpaginated file list capped at one hundred, reporting false violations on large pull requests.
The npm upgrade gate accepts an empty value for its node flag instead of refusing it as a usage error.
Lane grants naming a bundled source omit its generated mirrors, so every such edit forces a separate lane extension round trip.
The mirror sync check names no mirror paths on a clean tree, so it cannot enumerate the mirrors a lane should carry at declaration time.
An instrument census row names a neighbouring CI step as the consumer instead of the step that actually runs the gate.
A Makefile comment block describing one target sits above a different target after an insertion, misleading human readers.
The new agents instructions file has only a word-count cap, so false factual claims about the tree in it stay green.
The finish gate's verdict function prints without exiting, so a branch missing its exit emits a fail marker then falls through to ok.
Two tests assert a target name is absent by substring, so any new target whose name starts with it causes a false red.
The in-image battery target verifies each staged tool runs but discards the version output it warns matters for verdict parity.
The Makefile declaration reader loses a multi-target shared recipe when a later rule redeclares one of those targets, reading it as empty.
Three counter-model reviews in one wave ran without writing receipts, so the receipt corpus under-reports reviews that happened.
One control manifest uses a different prose key than all others, so a scripted amendment crashed and left unregistered fixture directories committed.
An issue's fixed helper population counts are stale against the currently derived population, risking an incomplete observation harness.
The wave registry list verb creates the wave mailbox directory as a side effect, fabricating evidence that a wave was set up.
The wave lexicon records a HOLD with no reason when the argument is written beneath the token, while reporting success.
The wave registry never prints the documented error verdict on usage errors, so callers filtering on the marker see silence.
A gate dedup feature refuses any Makefile with an include line, so a target designed on the assumption it applied would double test runs.
The PR watcher scrapes a negative control's deliberately echoed failures and reports them as pipeline failures, feeding the flake baseline.
The wave verdict ledger requires an issue number, so rulings on deliberately issueless fix work cannot be recorded or held.
The merge helper's closing-keyword guard missed a negated keyword in a markdown heading before an issue reference, so GitHub closed the issue.
The CI status helper reports an expired wait with no pipeline ever created the same as a not-yet-registered push, exiting zero for both.
The finish gate prints the counter-model receipt id and branch name concatenated without a separator, yielding an id matching no file.
An interrupted test run leaks a self-re-arming supervise daemon that no reaper collects across runs, spawning processes indefinitely.
Negative-control anchor messages label constructed anchors with a placeholder sha and omit the case name, making diagnostics unidentifiable.
Control GOOD cases for the finish gate read the ambient branch's receipt state, so verification goes red on any branch before its review receipt exists.
Count tripwire failure messages quoted a stale number disagreeing with their own assertions, and other prose counts remain unchecked.
Worktree removal depends on a record only the merge helper writes, and its refusal blames unpushed commits rather than the missing record.
The update command only adds helper symlinks and never prunes links whose targets were deleted upstream, leaving dangling stable paths.
The update command reports a model as missing when only an unreachable endpoint was observed, advising an unnecessary rebuild.
The registry list verb creates any wave directory it is asked about, so a mistyped wave name reads as a real but empty wave.
The toolchain provenance line dates the upstream fetch though the local checkout was stale, so readers discounted an exact count.
The install drift checker has no orphan category for helpers, so a dangling installed symlink is filtered out and it reports everything matches.
A supervise daemon outliving its session is reported as armed, and the duplicate refusal names no holder, so orphan debris blocks re-arming silently.
Correction locating the install drift orphan blindness in the source-side file test, so changing the other test would show no behaviour change.
The source-side regular-file test conflates absent entries with directories, so an orphan pass reusing it would flag a cache directory falsely.
The orphan pass needs different predicates on the install and source sides, and naive filters drop dangling symlinks while totals still reconcile.
The negative-control harness looks up its enumeration ADR at a fixed path, so repos filing it elsewhere print coverage counts against an unknown universe.
A command document claims a sender cannot distinguish a held cross-session message from a delivered one, but the harness now sends a hold notice.
The negative-control harness treats a non-zero exit as detection, so an anchor that crashes on every input is scored as correctly blind and passes.
A documented plan-comparison block captures NUL-separated paths via command substitution, merging multiple untracked paths and returning unknown.
The mailbox read consume mode does not acknowledge the boxes that peek displays, so the orchestrator's unread count never reaches zero.
The negative-control harness only discovers top-level scripts files, so a Make-target gate cannot be registered and the census omits the key gates.
The converged orphan predicate would flag host-owned scripts, contradicting a committed test, because orphanhood requires install provenance not existence.
Two fleet records give conflicting causes for held cross-session messages and neither references the other, so readers see only one.
A blinded anchor carries an undocumented path adaptation, so mechanical regeneration from the gate yields an anchor that crashes instead of missing.
An ADR census row lists a refusal verdict as sandbox-only after the gate gained refusals for git configuration problems.
On the host, the review tool's binary and its helper binary resolve from releases weeks apart because an older helper copy precedes it on PATH.
The code review command forces a read-only sandbox that cannot start in containers, so reviews silently run diff-only yet report success.
The mirror re-sync runs only when the base moved, but mirror drift comes from editing bundled files, so ordinary runs discover drift at the gate.
A declared PR on a wave roster entry cannot be cleared after it merges, so the roster keeps showing a stale pending PR.
A stand-down report claimed the watch stopped and the lane was released, but a watch process survived and the roster still showed unreleased entries.
The PR watcher treats any complete pytest summary region as authoritative, so a control's echoed summary still contaminates the failure list.
Delegated auto lanes create worktrees tracking the main branch, inviting a push to main, and their overrun check silently depends on that upstream.
The init command justifies its broadest permission profile by safety hooks that the project no longer ships.
